title: Out of the stone pillar
hookLine: a boon with every loophole closed, and a god who steps out of stone
carry: the Lord shows up to keep his devotee's word
tomorrow: the lion won't calm down. who dares walk up to him?

cards: A phone contract or a lease comes with pages of fine print, written so the company is covered whatever happens. Hiranyakashipu wrote fine print with a god.
Long before this night, after fierce austerities, he won a boon from Brahma, and he closed every loophole he could think of. Now, in the hall, the king strikes the pillar with his fist.
It splits open with a roar, and out steps something his list had no box for.

teach.b: Here's the fine print, as the Bhagavata Purana gives it. No death from any being Brahma created. Not by a human, not by an animal.
Not by day, not by night. Not on the ground, not in the sky. Not by any weapon.
Brahma grants it all. Now look at what steps out of the pillar.

teach.h: THE DOORWAY, THE DUSK, THE LAP.
teach.b: Narasimha: a body like a man's, a head like a lion's. Not a human, not an animal, and not made by Brahma. He carries the king to the threshold of the hall, neither inside nor outside.
The sun is going down: twilight. He lays the king across his lap, neither ground nor sky. No weapon, only claws.
Every word of the boon is kept. But the Bhagavata stops to say why he came this way, and that's the teaching.

teach.h: TO MAKE HIS DEVOTEE'S WORD TRUE.
teach.b: He came to make his devotee's words true, and to show that he is present in every being. Prahlada had said the Lord is everywhere.
The king picked the plainest, deadest thing in the room, a stone pillar, and the Lord was in that too.
This is the heart of what Hindus mean when they say God is everywhere: not only in the temple, but in stone, in an animal, in the person you'd least expect.
And it's why Narasimha is the form so many families call on for protection: the Lord who keeps his word to the one who trusts him.

how: Some Hindus keep Narasimha Jayanti at dusk, the hour of the story, and temple images sometimes show the moment in the doorway, the king across the man-lion's lap.

o: Vishnu as the man-lion who came out of a pillar
the twilight hour between day and night
the boon Brahma gave to the demon king

games.q: lock and loophole — tap the pairs.
p: a man's body, a lion's head
not on the ground or in the sky

s: Vishnu broke the terms of the boon to reach the king
every word is kept: the doorway, the dusk, the lap, no weapon.
Narasimha steps out of the pillar the king strikes
the king asked if Vishnu was in it, and the pillar answered.
Narasimha came only to punish the king
the Bhagavata says he came to make his devotee's words true, and to show he is in every being.

games.q: a friend sees a picture of Narasimha bursting out of a pillar and asks why Hindus tell it that way. what does the story answer?
o: to show the Lord is in everything, even stone, and keeps his devotee's word.
to show a god can always find a loophole in a deal.
because Vishnu happened to live inside that one pillar.
games.why: Prahlada said the Lord is everywhere. the king picked a stone pillar, and the Lord came out of it to prove the boy right.

practice: Some families pray to Narasimha for protection. If you pray, say quietly, a few times: om namo bhagavate narasimhaya, I bow to the Lord, Narasimha.
If you don't, rest a hand on something solid near you, a wall, a table, a doorframe, and hold the story's claim for a few slow breaths: not even this is empty.

wordCard.voice: Narasimha: the man-lion, who stepped out of a pillar to make a child's word true, and ended it at dusk.

orig.note: Sanskrit: twilight, the joining of day and night. Narasimha came at that hour.

carryVoice: For the road: the Lord shows up to keep his devotee's word. Even a stone pillar wasn't empty. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 7.3 (Hiranyakashipu's austerities; the boon from Brahma, 7.3.35–38)
Bhagavata Purana 7.8 (the pillar; why the Lord appears: to make his servant's word true and show his presence in all beings; the man-lion; the threshold; twilight; the lap; the nails)
